criteria.short: Fasst zusammen, was über die Herkunft und die Schulzeit des Erzählers zu erfahren ist
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling fasst zusammen, was über die Herkunft und die Schulzeit des Erzählers zu erfahren ist, etwa:
bullets: the narrator introduces himself as a freeborn of his village and as the only son of a single mother
he finished elementary school with an excellent result and describes himself as clever and hard-working
his mother could only finance his schooling with great difficulty
she was unable to pay the fees for secondary school
he had wanted to continue school in order to become a lawyer or a doctor

criteria.short: Fasst zusammen, wie sich der berufliche Weg des Erzählers entwickelt
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling fasst zusammen, wie sich der berufliche Weg des Erzählers entwickelt, etwa:
bullets: on his mother's advice he becomes an apprentice to the driver of the village lorry
the apprenticeship has to be paid for with money and additional goods
he learns the daily route from his village to the regional towns and back
he regards this work as a way to earn a licence, an own lorry and social advancement
he is proud of his job and spends part of his earnings on books to improve his English

criteria.short: Fasst zusammen, wie die politische Lage in das Leben des Erzählers eingreift
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling fasst zusammen, wie die politische Lage in das Leben des Erzählers eingreift, etwa:
bullets: while his village goes on celebrating, he realises that the country is drifting towards conflict
he criticises the villagers and the local authorities for their ignorance and self-interest
at a public assembly an official announces general mobilisation and conscription
the narrator is struck by a policeman during the meeting and reacts with fear and refusal

criteria.short: Entwickelt eine schlüssige These, die aufzeigt, wie die Charakterzeichnung des Erzählers, die Erzählperspektive und die sprachliche Gestaltung zusammenwirken, um Hoffnung und Spannung zu erzeugen
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling entwickelt eine schlüssige These, die aufzeigt, wie die Charakterzeichnung des Erzählers, die Erzählperspektive und die sprachliche Gestaltung zusammenwirken, um Hoffnung und Spannung zu erzeugen, z. B.:
bullets: the narrator's ambition, the naive first-person perspective and the pidgin idiom work together to create both hope and suspense
hope arises from the boy's belief in education and social advancement, e.g. becoming a “big man” (l. 8)
suspense arises from foreshadowing and the sudden shift from village routine to conscription
the gap between the boy's optimism and the reader's knowledge of the Biafra war produces dramatic irony

criteria.short: Analysiert die Charaktereigenschaften des Erzählers und belegt sie am Text
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling analysiert die Charaktereigenschaften des Erzählers und belegt sie am Text, z. B.:
bullets: ambitious: he dreams of becoming a “big man like lawyer or doctor” (l. 7-8)
hard-working and proud of his position: “I take my work serious” (l. 27)
eager to educate himself: he buys books in the motor park to improve his English (l. 30-31)
fatalistic when his plans collapse: “However, that is my luck” (l. 10)
naive yet observant: he mocks the villagers who “no get sense at all” (l. 34) while underestimating his own danger
fearful and unwilling once conscription is announced: “I cannot be a soza” (l. 60)

criteria.short: Analysiert, wie die Erzählperspektive Hoffnung und Spannung erzeugt
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling analysiert, wie die Erzählperspektive Hoffnung und Spannung erzeugt, z. B.:
bullets: narrative situation (nach Stanzel): first-person narrative situation, with the narrating I recalling the experiencing I
narrative point of view: the limited horizon of the uneducated boy creates dramatic irony, as readers recognise the approaching war earlier
time coverage: the excerpt spans years, from elementary school through the apprenticeship to general mobilisation
time lapse: iterative summary (“Every day”, l. 20) and omissions accelerate the account, while the assembly is told scenically and slows it down
foreshadowing: “if trouble begin proper, Dukana go see pepper” (l. 42) and “trouble done begin” (l. 49) announce the conflict
hope and suspense combined: his plans of licence and lorry (l. 15-17) keep hope alive, while the open ending leaves his fate unresolved

criteria.short: Analysiert, wie die sprachliche Gestaltung Hoffnung und Spannung erzeugt
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling analysiert, wie die sprachliche Gestaltung Hoffnung und Spannung erzeugt, z. B.:
bullets: “Rotten English” as a pidgin-based idiom marks the narrator's limited education: “I am prouding plenty” (l. 27)
reduplication intensifies and creates an oral tone: “big big English” (l. 8), “new new things” (l. 28)
Nigerian Pidgin and code-mixing add local colour: “chop money” (l. 14), “haba” (l. 51)
positive imagery evokes hope and peace: “It was beautiful new moon for Dukana” (l. 32)
the clash of registers makes the threat tangible: the official's “General mobilisation” (l. 53) against the boy's plain speech
simile and short elliptical sentences build suspense: “silent like burial ground” (l. 56), “My heart begins to cut” (l. 59)

criteria.short: Erörtert Saro-Wiwas Auffassung von der Rolle des Autors
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling erörtert Saro-Wiwas Auffassung von der Rolle des Autors, z. B.:
bullets: Saro-Wiwa rejects the idea of the writer as a “mere storyteller” and demands political engagement
literature is given a corrective function: it has to expose a society's weaknesses and dangers
the author is seen as an active participant in shaping the present and the future
writing is thus understood as a form of activism rather than as pure art
the position can be linked to Saro-Wiwa's own biography as a campaigner for the Ogoni people
counter-position: literature may lose its autonomy and turn into propaganda if it serves a political aim

criteria.short: Belegt seine Erörterung am vorliegenden Romanauszug
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling belegt seine Erörterung am vorliegenden Romanauszug, z. B.:
bullets: the novel exposes the recruitment of child soldiers and thus fulfils Saro-Wiwa's demand
the naive narrator lays bare the mechanisms of war propaganda, e.g. the official's inflated announcement (l. 50-55)
poverty and the lack of educational opportunities appear as social ills (l. 6-7)
local leaders are criticised as corrupt and without any plan (l. 39-40)
the use of “Rotten English” gives a literary voice to those usually excluded from written literature
the excerpt avoids open commentary, so its criticism works through the reader's own inference

criteria.short: Bezieht im Unterricht behandelte Reihen ein und kommt zu einem eigenen Urteil
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling bezieht im Unterricht behandelte Reihen ein und kommt zu einem eigenen Urteil, z. B.:
bullets: transfer to the dystopia unit: dystopian fiction likewise warns its readers by exposing political and social dangers
transfer to the drama unit: staged conflict confronts an audience directly and can trigger public debate
transfer to novel writing: narrative choices such as perspective and voice decide how strongly a text engages its readers
the comparison shows that committed literature is not limited to Nigeria but is a recurring function of literature
assessment: literature can raise awareness, yet its political effect remains indirect and hard to measure
own judgement, e.g. that Saro-Wiwa's demand is convincing for his historical context but too narrow as a general rule

criteria.short: Stellt die Hoffnungen und Träume des Protagonisten dar
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling stellt die Hoffnungen und Träume des Protagonisten dar, z. B.:
bullets: the speaker recalls his ambition to become a “big man” and to earn his own money as a driver
he hopes to obtain his own licence and later his own lorry in order to support Agnes and his mother
he dreams of a shared future in Dukana once the trouble in the country is over
he expresses his wish to go on reading and to improve his English
he imagines a life in which their children would be able to attend secondary school
he holds on to the hope of a better life in Nigeria itself

criteria.short: Stellt die Gefühle und Ängste des Protagonisten dar
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling stellt die Gefühle und Ängste des Protagonisten dar, z. B.:
bullets: he admits his fear of the announced mobilisation and of becoming a soldier
he describes the shock of the assembly, where the crowd suddenly fell silent
he fears that he may never return and that Agnes might not wait for him
he voices his sadness at leaving his mother behind without support
he feels torn between the demand to fight and his own refusal: “I cannot be a soza” (l. 60)
he confesses his uncertainty about how long the separation will last

criteria.short: Verknüpft den Brief mit der Romanvorlage und den Unterrichtsinhalten
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling verknüpft den Brief mit der Romanvorlage und den Unterrichtsinhalten, z. B.:
bullets: the letter stays consistent with the protagonist as characterised in the excerpt: ambitious, naive, devoted to his mother
it takes up his habit of making noise whenever he passes Agnes's home
it refers to hope for a better life in Nigeria, e.g. education and work as a way out of poverty
it addresses corruption as an obstacle, e.g. leaders who enrich themselves instead of protecting the village
it links the private farewell to the political situation of the country before the war
it keeps to the narrator's own horizon, without knowledge he could not possibly have

criteria.short: Gibt wieder, warum so viele junge Nigerianer nach Europa aufbrechen
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling gibt wieder, warum so viele junge Nigerianer nach Europa aufbrechen, etwa:
bullets: many young Africans are obsessed with the idea of Europe, which the psychologist calls a spreading epidemic
thousands of unscrupulous smugglers promise them everything imaginable
a lack of work and of prospects at home makes them set off towards the north
the movement is described as a mass phenomenon rather than an individual decision
the images of Europe circulating at home are unrealistic
Idemudia wants to keep young people from his home country from running into disaster

criteria.short: Gibt wieder, wie Idemudia das Leben von Nigerianern in Deutschland beschreibt
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling gibt wieder, wie Idemudia das Leben von Nigerianern in Deutschland beschreibt, etwa:
bullets: many Nigerians in Germany are unemployed and have no secure income
some end up dealing drugs or working as prostitutes
others do badly paid and low-status jobs, for example washing dishes in a restaurant
washing corpses is mentioned as another example of such work
the interview's headline suggests that Africans feel like aliens in Germany
Idemudia himself has friendly colleagues in Germany, so the picture is not entirely negative

criteria.short: Gibt wieder, warum die Wahrheit über die Lage in Deutschland zu Hause nicht ankommt
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling gibt wieder, warum die Wahrheit über die Lage in Deutschland zu Hause nicht ankommt, etwa:
bullets: most migrants are too proud to tell the truth about their situation
as a result nobody at home learns that they are unemployed
those doing menial jobs keep silent as well
no warnings therefore reach families and friends in Nigeria
the silence keeps the unrealistic image of Europe alive
Ikenna's friend would hardly hear about the risks from those already there

criteria.short: Gibt wieder, welche Alternativen und Lösungen Idemudia nennt
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling gibt wieder, welche Alternativen und Lösungen Idemudia nennt, etwa:
bullets: so far there is no objective and comprehensive study on African migrants in Europe
Idemudia is starting a new study in order to close this gap
he wants to approach the governments of Nigeria, Ghana and other countries with the results
public campaigns in the media, comparable to successful AIDS campaigns, are meant to inform young people
politics has to provide training, work and prospects at home, and scholarships could allow temporary stays in Europe without financial hardship
right-wing movements aggravate the problem, so lasting solutions need the EU and African governments together
